classification.difficultyReason: Link familiar circle-angle facts; the hardest part combines reflex-sector subtraction, equal-radius isosceles reasoning and halving a central angle.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Two radii form alpha; two circumference angles subtend the same lower-left arc. One is beta and the other is 42 degrees. Redundant letters are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The central sector is 84 degrees and the two inscribed angles on its arc are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only alpha, beta and the supplied 42-degree angle appear.

answer.worked:
$\beta=42^\circ$, because angles at the circumference subtended by the same arc are equal.
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=2\times42^\circ\\\alpha&=84^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The central angle is twice the circumference angle on that arc.

spec.description: Cyclic quadrilateral with a chord between the lower-left and lower-right vertices, two radii, top angle alpha, smaller central angle beta and bottom angle 118 degrees. Redundant letters are omitted.
spec.mathematics: Alpha is opposite 118 degrees. Beta is the central angle on the same lower arc as alpha.

answer.worked:
Opposite angles in the cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=180^\circ-118^\circ\\\alpha&=62^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The central angle is twice the circumference angle on the same arc.
$$\begin{aligned}\beta&=2\times62^\circ\\\beta&=124^\circ\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Three radii and three chords; reflex central angle 220 degrees, smaller lower central angle 66 degrees with a leader, supplied lower-right angle 57 degrees, and unknowns alpha and beta. Redundant letters are omitted.
spec.mathematics: Polar positions J=58 degrees, K=-16 degrees, I=-82 degrees give reflex JOI=220 degrees, IOK=66 degrees and OKI=57 degrees. Alpha lies between KJ and KO; beta lies between IK and IJ.
spec.answerVisibility: All three numerical givens remain; no calculated 74-degree central angle or answers are shown.

answer.short:
$\alpha=53^\circ,\quad\beta=37^\circ$.

Subtract the given central sectors, then use equal radii and the centre–circumference angle theorem.
answer.worked:
The smaller central angle between the upper and bottom radii is $360^\circ-220^\circ=140^\circ$.

The central angle between the upper and right radii is $140^\circ-66^\circ=74^\circ$.

The triangle formed by those two radii is isosceles, so
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=\frac{180^\circ-74^\circ}{2}\\\alpha&=53^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
The angle $\beta$ stands on the same arc as the $74^\circ$ central angle, so
$$\begin{aligned}\beta&=\frac{74^\circ}{2}\\\beta&=37^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
